categoryNotes.chatAgent: Registered, one-shot, by @codingame/monaco-vscode-api/services.js's unconditional `import "./missing-services.js"` (docs/research/2026-07-28-legacy-retirement.md "结论 1"): every Chat/Copilot/Agent service token missing-services.js does not find an installed override for gets a Null/default registerSingleton stub here, whether or not any of Plain's 13 real override packages ever reference it (结论 2 confirmed 12/13 are clean; the scm-service-override exception was already known not to reach the real bundle). 121 of these 122 are workbench/contrib/{chat,inlineChat,agentEditorComments}/** or platform/agentHost/** stub/token files. The 122nd, workbench/contrib/remoteCodingAgents/common/remoteCodingAgentsService.service.js, was found during F110 S0's real-content audit: its stub (registerAgent/getRegisteredAgents/getAvailableAgents, all no-ops) sits in missing-services.js directly between ChatAttachmentResolveService and McpElicitationService and is genuinely an AI coding-agent registry despite the 'remote' spelling in its directory name -- classifying it under a bare remote keyword match would have repeated the exact globalCompositeBar.js filename-vs-content mismatch this research flagged as a trap. Expected floor after F110 S3: 0.

categoryNotes.extensionRuntime: The most heterogeneous category (docs/research/2026-07-28-legacy-retirement.md "结论 2"): 34 are @codingame/monaco-vscode-api base-package missing-services.js stubs/tokens (e.g. extensions.js's NullExtensionService), but 13 are real, instantiated @codingame/monaco-vscode-extensions-service-override files (extensionService.js's real ExtensionServiceOverride, rpcProtocol.js, extensionHostManager.js, etc.) -- already deeply neutered by patches/@codingame__monaco-vscode-extensions-service-override@35.0.1.patch (DisabledExtensionHostFactory/DisabledExtensionHostKindPicker) so no host of any kind can ever be created, but the files and their RPC/lifecycle scaffolding remain. The main session's decision point 3 ruling accepts a non-zero floor here (replacing the vendor IExtensionService DI token is judged too risky for the benefit); F110 S5's evidence must enumerate whatever floor remains file-by-file with a behavioral-inertness argument for each, not just a total.

note: F110 S0 (docs/research/2026-07-28-legacy-retirement.md, decision points 4/5): this baseline is a ratchet, not a fixed value. scripts/plain/check-bundle.mjs fails a category only when its real debt-source count exceeds categoryCeilings[category], or when it contains a source path never catalogued in debtSources for that category before -- either signals a regression. A category shrinking (fewer or zero real members, all already present in debtSources) passes without editing this file; that is deliberate, so later F110 cleanup slices are never tempted to mask a regression by hand-editing a number. debtSources is the explicit, machine-generated floor list acceptance #5's own research called for ("哪些文件还在、各自为什么还在") -- see categoryNotes per category for why each group is still present and when it is expected to reach its floor. The previous schema (schemaVersion 1) locked debtSourceCount/categoryCounts to exact values plus a debtSourceSha256 of the joined debt-source list; that exact-match semantics is incompatible with a ratchet (any real decrease changes the hash, which would force a manual baseline edit on every legitimate cleanup -- the same 'edit the number to make it green' anti-pattern the ratchet exists to remove), so debtSourceSha256 has been dropped rather than kept as dead weight. debtSources supersedes it: unlike a hash, it is diffable, human-readable, and (via the per-category subset check) still catches a same-count swap of one tracked debt source for a different, previously-untracked one, which a bare numeric ceiling alone would miss.
